clue.text: Hard — of skin or heart

parts.note: the one adjective covers both thickened, hardened skin and an unfeeling, hard-hearted nature

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss on hardness of body and of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hardened, whether of skin toughened by friction or of a person grown unfeeling.

clue.text: Bear and cat involved in a show

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the two animals' letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bear and a cat take part in a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is entertainment staged in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Tall winner in American parlance, of course in France

parts.note: long means tall in height
champ is the American informal word for a champion

explanation.surface: A tall American champion, and a French racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Longchamp is the racecourse in Paris's Bois de Boulogne, home of the Arc de Triomphe race.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Parisian horse-racing venue.

clue.text: It's not the same in radiotherapy

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the medical word

explanation.surface: A remark that something differs in cancer treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something different, not identical, is something else.

clue.text: Firm is among those who send supporters

indicators.note: is among tells us the firm goes inside the senders

parts.note: senders are people who send
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company is among those who dispatch backers.
explanation.definitionFit: People who formally back a motion in a meeting.

clue.text: Establishment in which record business might be done ?

definitions.text: Establishment in which record business might be done ?

parts.words: Establishment in which record business might be done
parts.note: reads as a shop selling chart records, but 'pop' is slang for pawning, and a pawnshop does record business of its own

explanation.surface: A record store where hit singles are sold.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'pop' something is old British slang for pawning it, so a pop shop is a pawnbroker's, which the surface disguises as a music shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang name for a pawnbroker's premises, where goods are pledged for loans.

clue.text: Presumably not the motorist's favourite flowers

definitions.text: Presumably not the motorist's favourite flowers

parts.words: Presumably not the motorist's favourite flowers
parts.note: a motorist dislikes an engine that knocks, a fault called pinking, which shares its name with these flowers

explanation.surface: Blooms drivers are unlikely to like.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinking is the British term for an engine knocking from premature ignition, so a motorist would not favour it.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden flowers of the carnation family.

clue.text: Work that provides the writer with a hot dinner?

definitions.text: Work that provides the writer with a hot dinner?

parts.words: Work that provides the writer with a hot dinner
parts.note: a book written only to earn money keeps the pot on the boil, putting a meal on the writer's table

explanation.surface: Writing that pays for the writer's meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A hack book written chiefly to earn a living, keeping the pot on the boil.

clue.text: A little colouring gives a bird an uplift!

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: in a down clue an uplift turns the word upward, so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: A dab of dye raises a bird's spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish dye from a shrub, used to tint hair and skin.

clue.text: But not the politician's first job

definitions.text: But not the politician's first job

parts.words: But not the politician's first job
parts.note: first suggests a beginner's post, but the word that means first is also the title of the top political job

explanation.surface: A remark that this is not a politician's earliest post.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means first or leading, and it is also the title of a prime minister, which is never a politician's first job.
explanation.definitionFit: Means foremost, and is the title of a head of government.

clue.text: Not that the Queen sits on hers

definitions.text: Not that the Queen sits on hers

parts.words: Not that the Queen sits on hers
parts.note: a seat for sitting, though the Queen's is the court called the Queen's ..., not furniture she uses

explanation.surface: A remark that the monarch does not actually sit on a certain seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen's Bench is a division of the English High Court, named for the monarch but not sat on by her.
explanation.definitionFit: A long seat, and also the name for a court or the judges sitting in it.

clue.text: Lady of the Lake ?

parts.note: evokes the Arthurian enchantress, but means a woman's name that is also the name of a lake

explanation.surface: The Arthurian Lady of the Lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake Constance lies between Germany, Switzerland and Austria, and Constance is also a woman's name, so the 'lady' shares the lake's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name which is also the English name of the Bodensee.

clue.text: Not payments for carrying luggage by train

definitions.text: Not payments for carrying luggage by train

parts.words: Not payments for carrying luggage by train
parts.note: suggests fees for using a carriage's luggage rack, but means extortionate rents

explanation.surface: A remark about luggage charges on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: A rack-rent is an excessive rent; the clue pretends it means a charge for space on a train's luggage rack.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant rents squeezed out of tenants, the landlord 'racking' them.

clue.text: It's all right with a good animal

parts.note: OK is an informal way of saying all right
PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone approving of a well-behaved creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A giraffe-like forest mammal of central Africa.

clue.text: A sign of harness

definitions.meaning: a mark or vestige left behind
the straps by which a horse pulls a cart

explanation.definitionFit: Both a slight indication left behind and one of the side straps of a draught horse's harness.

clue.text: It's hard on the pupils

parts.note: pupils suggests schoolchildren, but means the openings of the eye

explanation.surface: Something tough for schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue of the eyes from overuse.

clue.text: A romantic blade

parts.note: suggests a dashing young man, but means a sword from romance, the medieval tales of chivalry

explanation.surface: A dashing young gallant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blade' can mean a dashing man, but here it is a sword; 'romantic' refers to the Arthurian romances.
explanation.definitionFit: King Arthur's sword in the medieval legends.

clue.text: Was Jack Horner one of these minstrel show types ?

definitions.text: Was Jack Horner one of these minstrel show types ?

parts.words: Was Jack Horner one of these minstrel show types
parts.note: Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme sat in a corner; the end performers of a minstrel line share the name

explanation.surface: A question whether a nursery-rhyme boy was a stage performer.
explanation.walkthrough: In the rhyme 'Little Jack Horner sat in the corner'; in a minstrel show the comic end men were also called corner men.
explanation.definitionFit: The performers at each end of a minstrel troupe's line.

clue.text: Failure in this game entails being out of pocket

definitions.text: Failure in this game entails being out of pocket

parts.words: Failure in this game entails being out of pocket
parts.note: out of pocket means losing money, but in this cue sport failure means the ball stays out of the pocket

explanation.surface: Losing at a game costs money.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue game played on a cloth table with pockets.

clue.text: Prospero's become a tyrant

indicators.note: the letters of the magician's name turn into a new arrangement, as one thing becomes another

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's magician in The Tempest has turned despot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prospero's' is Prospero has, and its S counts in the fodder; 'become' rearranges PROSPEROS.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressive ruler is one who rules cruelly, which is what a despot does.

clue.text: Cleopatra's rival changes her coat the Roman way

indicators.note: changes says the letters of coat are switched around

parts.note: via is Latin for road or way

explanation.surface: Cleopatra's rival alters her coat in the Roman fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Octavia, sister of Octavian, was Mark Antony's wife and so Cleopatra's rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Antony's Roman wife, whom he left for the Egyptian queen.

clue.text: Baker, their master ?

parts.note: a baker is master of the bread he bakes, as a car maker's name might suggest a master of cars

explanation.surface: A baker named as the master of some unnamed group.
explanation.walkthrough: The baker is master of bread rolls; there may also be a nod to the master of the Rolls, a senior English judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Small loaves of bread made by a baker.

clue.text: They indicate that jargon is back

indicators.note: is back says the run of words is read in reverse

parts.note: slang is informal jargon

explanation.surface: Signs show that technical talk is returning.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs or gestures that convey information.

clue.text: Doctrine appealing to mr Facing-both-ways?

indicators.note: Mr Facing-both-ways in Pilgrim's Progress looks both ways, so he would like a word that reads the same in either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A creed that would suit a two-faced character.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Facing-both-ways is a character in Bunyan's Pilgrim's Progress who sides with whoever suits him.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief held as true by a group.

clue.text: Men on certain occasions revealing the present one

indicators.note: revealing tells us the word is exposed inside the run of words

explanation.surface: Men on particular occasions show the current one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the nonce' means for the present occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: The present occasion or time, as in the phrase about the time being.

clue.text: It makes a gripping spectacle

parts.note: gripping means thrilling in the surface but literally holding opponents fast here

explanation.surface: A show that holds the audience spellbound.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat sport where opponents grapple and hold each other.

clue.text: It was their turn to play or sing

definitions.text: It was their turn to play or sing

parts.words: It was their turn to play or sing
parts.note: the street musicians who played or sang carols at Christmas, a 'turn' being a performance

explanation.surface: Performers whose turn has come.
explanation.walkthrough: Waits were bands of street singers and players who went from house to house at Christmas in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of carol singers and players going round at Christmas.

clue.text: Reduce that light, when turning fearful

indicators.note: turning means the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: to dim it is to reduce that light

explanation.surface: Lower that lamp when the nerves turn jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking courage, easily scared.

clue.text: Action by ancient or modern destroyers

definitions.text: Action by ancient or modern destroyers

parts.words: Action by ancient or modern destroyers
parts.note: the Vandals were an ancient tribe who sacked Rome, and modern vandals wreck property

explanation.surface: Destructive behaviour across the ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilful damage to property, named after the Germanic tribe that sacked Rome.

clue.text: Black girl giving a lift to those in trouble

definitions.text: Black girl giving a lift to those in trouble

parts.words: Black girl giving a lift to those in trouble
parts.note: a girl's name which follows 'black' to name the police van that carries arrested people

explanation.surface: A woman helping out people in difficulty by driving them.
explanation.walkthrough: A Black Maria is British slang for a police van; it gives a 'lift' to people in trouble with the law.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, completing the slang term for a prison van.

clue.text: Where the descent is hellishly easy

definitions.text: Where the descent is hellishly easy

parts.words: Where the descent is hellishly easy
parts.note: echoes Virgil's line that the descent to the underworld is easy, by way of a lake near Naples

explanation.surface: A slope so easy to go down that it seems devilish.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's Aeneid says 'facilis descensus Averno': the way down to hell is easy. The lake near Naples was held to be the entrance to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater lake in Campania that the ancients called the gateway to the underworld.

clue.text: They have no fear of exposure

definitions.text: They have no fear of exposure

parts.words: They have no fear of exposure
parts.note: exposure suggests a scandal or the cold, but means baring the body

explanation.surface: People unafraid of being found out.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists, who go about unclothed by choice.
